sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict confirmed_shifted: insert_after_residue 173 -> 178 on human canonical Q02297 (paper numbering: isoform:NRG1 type III (700 aa), construct species: unstated). Paper (PMID 38136627): "HA-tag (amino-acid residues: YPYDVPDYA ...) was inserted into amino-acid residue 233-234 of Nrg1 type III". Audit note: In the 700-aa type III isoform (human A0A494C0Q4 and mouse Q6DR99 agree locally) residues 233|234 are H|L in ...TGTSH|LVKCAEK, the first residues of the EGF-like domain. In canonical Q02297 that junction is H178|L179, so the offset is -55, not the ~-60 the row assumed; the row's T173|T174 is 5 residues upstream. Type III has no Ig domain, so 'between Ig and EGF' is wrong. HA was used for IP/western only.] L1 names residues 233-234 of NRG1 type III as the HA insertion site. NRG1 type III (700 aa) differs from the canonical type I (640 aa) by an N-terminal CRD domain of approximately 60 aa; subtracting this offset gives canonical equivalent ~173-174. Python computation confirms pos 173 = T and pos 174 = T in the canonical sequence, both extracellular (EC 1-242) and 69 residues from the TM boundary (243). The exact offset is uncertain (58-62 aa), so position_evidence is 'inferred' and cited_tag_residue is set to 233 (the type III residue actually cited). This site is consistent with the region-level evidence in L7/L8. L1 (PMC10741733) reports an HA tag inserted at residues 233-234 of NRG1 type III (700 aa) in the full-length membrane-anchored construct p3xFlag-HA-Myc-Nrg1 type III. NRG1 type III carries an N-terminal CRD domain (~60 aa) absent from the canonical type I isoform (640 aa); subtracting this offset maps type III pos 233 to canonical pos ~173. Pos 173 (T) is in the extracellular stalk between the Ig-like and EGF-like domains, consistent with L7/L8 which independently describe an HA insertion 'between Ig and EGF domains' in a full-length NRG1 construct.

sites.rationale: L7 and L8 name the Ig-EGF domain boundary as the insertion site for an HA tag in a full-length membrane-anchored NRG1 construct expressed in transgenic mice. In the canonical type I sequence (640 aa), the Ig-like domain spans approximately residues 1-50 and the EGF-like domain spans approximately 176-226 (extracellular, well within EC 1-242); the intervening stalk (roughly 51-175) is the Ig-EGF linker. No residue number is given in either clip, so insert_after_residue is left null and the site is reported at region level. L7 and L8 (PMC7804852) report that an HA tag was inserted 'between the Ig and EGF domains' of NRG1 in a full-length construct expressed in gtoNrg1 transgenic mice. HA immunostaining in brain sections confirmed expression of the tagged construct. No specific residue number is given in either clip; the site is named only at the domain-boundary level.

sites.rationale: The canonical NRG1 type I sequence has no signal peptide and the N-terminus (pos 1, M) is directly extracellular (EC 1-242). L3 explicitly confirms via non-permeabilized immunostaining that the N-terminal FLAG tag of the full-length membrane-anchored NRG1 type III construct is displayed on the cell surface. Because the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus of this single-pass type I topology, insert_after_residue=0 (prepend) is the only possible junction; residue_after is M (pos 1). L9, L10/L11/L12, and L5/L6 provide convergent corroboration across human and zebrafish NRG1 isoforms. Full-length NRG1 type III (700 aa) cloned into p3xFlag-Myc-24 with 3xFLAG at the N-terminus (L2); non-permeabilized anti-FLAG immunostaining of transfected cells confirmed the N-terminal tag is displayed on the extracellular face (L3). The canonical type I sequence (640 aa) has no signal peptide and the same type I topology (EC 1-242), so the N-terminus is directly extracellular. Multiple additional ledger lines (L9: two HA tags at N-terminus of NRG1 used in myelination studies; L10/L11/L12: N-terminal HA on CRD-NRG1 in transgenic mice; L5/L6: mCherry near N-terminus of zebrafish NRG1Iβ1 with confirmed surface localization) all corroborate N-terminal tagging of full-length membrane-bound NRG1 constructs.
